messages.subject: Reproportion circular tree
messages.body_plain:
I have created a circular tree using ggtree with symbols for each sequence. Currently, the branches are rather long and the symbols are overlapping making the tree difficult to read. I would like to enlarge the center space of the tree to separate the symbols and to make the tree easier to read, but I am having trouble finding the right command. Is there any way to increase the percentage of the circles that is occupied by white space in the center? Any help is greatly appreciated.

Kind regards, Kirston

messages.subject: Re: Reproportion circular tree
messages.body_plain:
try using xlim to allocate space in the center.

require(ggtree)

set.seed(2016-03-15)
tr=rtree(50)
p = ggtree(tr, layout='circular')
p2 = p + xlim(-5, NA)
multiplot(p, p2, ncol=2)

messages.subject: collapse and gheatmap
messages.body_plain:
Using gheatmap the convenient tool, I can generate a heatmap associated to a phylogeny. On the other hand, I can also collapse part of my tree with collapse the function, but in the mean time I cannot apply gheatmap to the collapsed tree.
Is it possible that when part of my tree is collapsed, heatmap values corresponding to the collapsed part can also be accumulated, and thus the collapsed node can be presented as sum values of the collapsed data in the associated heatmap?
If it's not available, may you please suggest alternative approaches?

messages.subject: Re: collapse and gheatmap
messages.body_plain:
this is currently not available. Using sum value is misleading. max, min, or average are better than using sum. But we can't apply these numerical functions to categorical variable which is also very common, as we demonstrated in the vignette which use a genotype matrix.

The best way in my opinion is to set the collapsed node to NA, which should work in current implementation.

messages.subject: Re: Facet Wrap of the same tree with different annotations
messages.subject_clean: Facet Wrap of the same tree with different annotations
messages.body_plain:
p <- ggtree(tree) %<+% df

p + facet_wrap(~sites) + geom_tippoint(aes(value))

This is not meaningful for phylogenetic tree, since facet_wrap(~sites) will split the data by ~sites and plot each sub-dataset in subpanel, while all the sub-datasets don't contain a whole tree structure.

It's only possible if we duplicate the underlying data and modify the ~sites column for subset while adding an additional column for facet.

Here is an example:

library(ggtree)
nwk <- system.file("extdata", "sample.nwk", package="ggtree")
tree <- read.tree(nwk)
p <- ggtree(tree)

dd <- data.frame(taxa  = LETTERS[1:13],
                 place = c(rep("GZ", 5), rep("HK", 3), rep("CZ", 4), NA),
                 value = round(abs(rnorm(13, mean=70, sd=10)), digits=1))

place <- c("CZ", "GZ", "HK")

p = ggtree(tree) %<+% dd
p$data <- lapply(place, function(x) {
    d <- p$data
    d$site <- x
    d$place[d$place != x] = NA
    d
}) %>% do.call('rbind', .)

p + facet_wrap(~site) + geom_point2(aes(size=value, subset=!is.na <http://is.na>(place)))

messages.subject_clean: Facet Wrap of the same tree with different annotations
messages.body_plain:
another solution is to produce separate figures and use multiplot to visualize them.

p = ggtree(tree) %<+% dd

p1 = p + geom_point2(aes(size=value, subset=(place %in% "CZ")))
p2 = p + geom_point2(aes(size=value, subset=(place %in% "GZ")))
p3 = p + geom_point2(aes(size=value, subset=(place %in% "HK")))
multiplot(p1, p2, p3, ncol=3, labels=c("CZ", "GZ", "HK"))

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-TwlJmgFsRCY/VvpN39frYKI/AAAAAAAAAbU/kzFpn0cbHJYUHSnGCzHhNxVxHpV6Ag9nw/s1600/Screenshot%2B2016-03-29%2B17.40.37.png>
